review_notes: I read the whole file and the related uses of mulLLift and mulRLift in sibling files. The only simp-interface issue I found is the missing projection lemmas for the two lift definitions. The other declarations (abbrevs, `genericInclusion_comp`, the integrality theorems) have no simp-related issues I could justify. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that the proposed lemmas compile or that they would shorten the proofs by a specific amount.

findings.excerpt:
def mulRLift : X3 q ⟶ pullback q q :=
  pullback.lift (fst₃ q ≫ pullback.fst q q)
findings.problem: `mulLLift` and `mulRLift` are plain `def`s over `pullback.lift`, and no `fst`/`snd` projection lemmas are provided for them. Every proof that touches them has to unfold the definition with `simp only [mulLLift, ...]` or `simp only [mulRLift, ...]`. Unfolding exposes the whole `pullback.lift` body, so the following `pullback.lift_fst` and `pullback.lift_snd` rewrites have to rediscover the components each time. The same pattern appears in `mulL_over`, `mulR_over` and both `hfac` blocks of `mulL_eq_mulR'`. It is also repeated in two sibling files, so the missing canonical simp lemmas cost every user.
findings.proposed_change: Add projection lemmas right after each definition, for example `@[reassoc (attr := simp)] lemma mulLLift_fst : mulLLift q m hm ≫ pullback.fst q q = fst₃ q ≫ m := pullback.lift_fst _ _ _`, and likewise `mulLLift_snd`, `mulRLift_fst` and `mulRLift_snd`. The `_assoc` versions come from `reassoc`. The `mulRLift_snd` right-hand side is `pullback.lift (fst₃ q ≫ pullback.snd q q) (snd₃ q) (pr₂_over q) ≫ m`. Callers can then use `simp [mulLLift_fst, ...]` or `rw` and no longer need `simp only [mulLLift, ...]`. Each lemma should have the lift on the left and its components on the right, so the rewrite is terminating and keeps the definition opaque to simp.
findings.benefit: The definitions become a stable rewrite interface in the same style as `pullback.lift_fst` and `pullback.lift_snd`. Proofs such as `mulL_over`, `mulR_over` and the two `hfac` blocks stop depending on the internal construction. Nothing would be unfolded implicitly, and downstream files could reuse the lemmas instead of repeating the unfolding.
